headlines: Real Blocker Ranking: Gating analysis across restricted platforms reveals app_review (11), self_hosted_per_instance (4), thin_or_unclear_docs (4) as the primary architectural bottlenecks. Managed OAuth scopes and partner review queues represent the highest integration friction.

Portfolio Velocity Split: 63 Easy Wins (self-serve free/trial APIs) vs 15 Outreach Targets (gated behind partner reviews or sales agreements) vs 18 Configuration-Dependent (paid/self-hosted/admin) vs 4 CLI/No-API Tools (Total: 100).
Authentication Architecture by Category: CRM & Messaging mandate OAuth2 (9/10 CRM apps), whereas Developer Infra & Scraping rely primarily on API Keys (5/10 Dev apps) for headless machine execution.
Catalog Feasibility: 69 apps immediately buildable today, 28 requiring partner provisioning or containerized execution, and 3 lacking public developer APIs.

needs_outreach.name: DealCloud
needs_outreach.reason: DealCloud provides a well-documented REST API and Python/C# SDKs supporting standard authentication methods like OAuth2 client credentials and API keys. However, access is enterprise-gated, requiring contact with sales to provision tenant environments.

needs_outreach.name: Zoho Cliq
needs_outreach.reason: Zoho Cliq provides a REST API accessible via Zoho's API console and OAuth server-based applications. Developers can self-serve trial accounts and create console integrations, making it buildable with effort (yellow) due to OAuth setup requirements.

needs_outreach.name: Lark (Larksuite)
needs_outreach.reason: Lark provides extensive REST APIs across multiple modules via Custom Apps. Building tools requires initial developer configuration including app scope assignment, regional cloud selection (larksuite vs feishu), and tenant release approval.

needs_outreach.name: WhatsApp Business
needs_outreach.reason: WhatsApp Business API is buildable with yellow verdict due to Meta business verification and system user token prerequisites. Developers can obtain credentials via Meta Business Manager or BSPs, making integration manageable though requiring setup effort.

needs_outreach.name: Google Ads
needs_outreach.reason: Google Ads provides robust REST API capabilities with self-serve test accounts, but production usage requires developer token approval and strict adherence to Google Ads API terms, creating friction for multi-tenant OAuth managed applications.

needs_outreach.name: Meta Ads
needs_outreach.reason: Meta Ads provides robust self-serve developer access and a development mode sandbox for building integrations, but requires formal Business Verification and App Review (Advanced Access) before managing production ad accounts for external clients.

needs_outreach.name: LinkedIn Ads
needs_outreach.reason: LinkedIn Marketing API requires developer app creation and a multi-step review process (including a video submission for Standard tier). While fully buildable, shipping a production multi-tenant OAuth app requires passing LinkedIn's developer app review.

needs_outreach.name: Threads (Meta)
needs_outreach.reason: Threads provides a self-serve developer portal on Meta, but multi-tenant production use for all external users requires passing Meta App Review for permissions like threads_content_publish.

needs_outreach.name: Shopify
needs_outreach.reason: Shopify provides powerful GraphQL and REST APIs with standard OAuth authentication, making it buildable today. However, distributing a public multi-tenant app requires app review and partner program compliance.

needs_outreach.name: Squarespace
needs_outreach.reason: Squarespace provides extensive REST APIs with OpenAPI documentation for commerce management, orders, and products. While individual developers can use merchant API keys on Advanced plans, building a managed multi-tenant OAuth integration requires manual client registration and review by Squarespace, resulting in a yellow buildability verdict.

needs_outreach.name: Amazon Selling Partner
needs_outreach.reason: Amazon SP-API provides robust REST APIs with OpenAPI models, but requires strict developer registration, role qualifications, and partner-gated onboarding, presenting friction for native multi-tenant platform integration.

needs_outreach.name: Plaid
needs_outreach.reason: The official MCP server in plaid/ai-coding-toolkit exposes local developer/sandbox tooling (custom test users, mock data generation, test token generation, and doc search). It does NOT expose production banking data. For Composio production financial toolkits, access to real customer accounts is gated behind Plaid Production compliance review and Link OAuth.

needs_outreach.name: QuickBooks
needs_outreach.reason: QuickBooks is already supported in Composio, but Intuit developer setup involves rigorous app review and compliance processes for production multi-tenant OAuth access.

needs_outreach.name: PitchBook
needs_outreach.reason: PitchBook provides no public self-serve developer documentation or API endpoints on its main website, requiring users to contact sales or request a trial, making integration building currently blocked.

needs_outreach.name: Consensus
needs_outreach.reason: The retrieved documentation page contains only marketing copy for Consensus as a research tool without any developer portal, API reference, or authentication endpoints.

requires_configuration.name: Pylon
requires_configuration.reason: Pylon provides well-documented REST APIs using simple API token bearer authentication which can be generated directly by workspace admins. Developers can easily build integrations today.

requires_configuration.name: Gorgias
requires_configuration.reason: Gorgias provides standard REST APIs with both private API keys and OAuth2 authentication, making it fully buildable for integrations and agent tools.

requires_configuration.name: Gladly
requires_configuration.reason: Gladly provides a well-documented REST API and OpenAPI specification with token-based basic auth. However, because API endpoints are hosted at per-organization domains ({organization}.gladly.com) and use organization-specific credentials, building a generic multi-tenant integration requires handling dynamic base URLs.

requires_configuration.name: Aircall
requires_configuration.reason: Aircall provides a robust public REST API with self-serve API keys generated directly from the dashboard for user accounts, making it green for development. While multi-tenant OAuth requires contacting marketplace@aircall.io, individual developer access is straightforward via Basic Auth.

requires_configuration.name: GoHighLevel
requires_configuration.reason: GoHighLevel provides both self-serve Private Integration Tokens (PIT) for direct account access and OAuth 2.0 for multi-tenant integrations. Standard API access is available across subscription plans, making it fully ready to build.

requires_configuration.name: WooCommerce
requires_configuration.reason: WooCommerce is a self-hosted open-source e-commerce platform running on WordPress, requiring each merchant store instance URL and generated consumer keys/secrets to connect via REST API.

requires_configuration.name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
requires_configuration.reason: Salesforce Commerce Cloud provides standard REST APIs secured via OAuth/Bearer tokens, but requires enterprise subscriptions and specific instance/site IDs to configure API clients. While buildable, setting up multi-tenant OAuth or connecting requires paid enterprise access and proper Account Manager credentials.

requires_configuration.name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
requires_configuration.reason: Magento (Adobe Commerce) is a self-hosted or cloud-instance e-commerce platform requiring a per-instance base URL and admin-generated OAuth 1.0a credentials. While fully buildable for REST and GraphQL, it is classified as yellow because it is a self-hosted/per-instance application rather than a uniform multi-tenant SaaS.

requires_configuration.name: SE Ranking
requires_configuration.reason: SE Ranking provides well-documented REST APIs across multiple domains (backlinks, rankings, site audits, AI search visibility) with self-serve API keys obtainable directly from the dashboard. Developers can easily integrate tools using API key authentication, and there is an official MCP repository available.

requires_configuration.name: Ahrefs
requires_configuration.reason: Ahrefs features a well-documented REST API v3 with an OpenAPI spec and an official hosted MCP server. However, API v3 access requires an Enterprise subscription ($1,499/mo), which creates high pricing friction for end users.

requires_configuration.name: Clay
requires_configuration.reason: Clay offers self-serve trials and agent plugins, but public API/documentation details are minimal on the marketing page, placing it at a yellow buildability rating pending deeper API docs.

requires_configuration.name: Neo4j
requires_configuration.reason: External documentation pages for Neo4j could not be retrieved, leading to limited verification of exact endpoints. However, as a database/infrastructure tool, it typically requires per-instance connection parameters making it a yellow buildability candidate.

requires_configuration.name: Snowflake
requires_configuration.reason: Snowflake is a cloud data platform requiring instance-specific account identifiers and credentials to connect. It is already supported in Composio, and developers can easily sign up for a trial account to test integrations.

requires_configuration.name: Binance
requires_configuration.reason: Binance is buildable with self-serve API keys and testnet environments, but requires handling request signing (HMAC) and potential regional or KYC restrictions for live accounts.

requires_configuration.name: Paygent Connect
requires_configuration.reason: Ambiguous entity: hint specifies NMI-powered gateway, but no public developer API or documentation exists under Paygent Connect. Marked low confidence.

requires_configuration.name: Ramp
requires_configuration.reason: Ramp provides machine-readable documentation and a full OpenAPI specification at /openapi/developer-api.json, making it straightforward to integrate into Composio.

requires_configuration.name: Reducto
requires_configuration.reason: Reducto offers document parsing and an Office SDK with a free trial option, but the provided text lacks deep API documentation or explicit endpoint listings, resulting in yellow buildability pending full API docs.

requires_configuration.name: Devin
requires_configuration.reason: Devin provides an API and web platform requiring an individual or team plan. Detailed public API endpoints and specs are lacking in the base documentation, making integration moderately effort-intensive.

top_15_build_order.reasoning: Pumble provides an API addon that allows generating workspace API keys for integrations. Developers can self-serve access via the workspace UI, making it buildable with yellow friction due to requiring the addon installation steps.

top_15_build_order.reasoning: MrScraper is ready to integrate immediately with API tokens available via self-serve dashboard access, including a free tier. It already maintains an official open-source MCP server on GitHub.

top_15_build_order.name: Otter AI

top_15_build_order.reasoning: Otter.ai provides an official OAuth-authenticated Model Context Protocol (MCP) server accessible directly in Claude connectors, as well as a documented Public REST API for Enterprise workspaces.
